An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 8 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 9 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 10 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 11 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 12 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 13 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 14 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 15 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 16 17 API 18 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 19 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 22 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 23 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 24 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 25 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 26 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 27 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 28 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 29 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 30 31 Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 32 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 33 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 34 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 35 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 36 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 37 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 38 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 39 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 40 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 41 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. 42 - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. 43 44 Page 45 - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. 46 - The page loads the script with a `

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

content.text:
I graded both new files against every line of the spec's Page section (lines 44-61). They pass with 9/10. Your fake-DOM check (`node /tmp/fe-check/check.mjs`) prints `ALL OK`, and a grep of both files finds none of the banned items: no `http://` or `https://`, no `innerHTML`, `createTextNode`, `querySelector`, `setAttribute`, `classList`, `res.ok`, `console`, `import` or `export`, and no `<option>` or room names in the HTML.

**Spec compliance (all met)**
- **HTML** (`/root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/public/index.html`):
  - The title and the only `<h1>` read `Room bookings`.
  - The form has `novalidate`. All five fields carry the right ids, names and types, and each has its own separate label with the exact text.
  - The filter input and its label sit outside the form. `#show-all` has `type="button"`, and `#error` has `role="alert"` and is empty.
  - `<script src="/app.js">` has no extra attributes and is the last element in `<body>`. There is no inline script and no `on...` attribute; the `<style>` block is allowed.
- **Script** (`/root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/public/app.js`):
  - It only uses the allowed browser APIs. The other things it uses are plain JavaScript (`Array.isArray`, `JSON.stringify`).
  - Replies: a 204 body is never read, and any other reply whose body won't parse as JSON counts as no reply. The message is the body's `error` value when it is a string, otherwise `Request failed.`
  - The list fetch uses a sequence counter, so only the last one started can change the list or `#error`. It adds `?date=` with the value unchanged, builds two child nodes per `<li>` with no trailing space, and shows a single `No bookings.` item when there are none.
  - Booking: `preventDefault` runs first, a submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing, and the title is sent untrimmed with exactly one `Content-Type` header. `Book` is enabled again before anything else, and on 201 only the title is cleared, `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again.
  - Cancel fetches the list again on 204 or an error status, but not when there is no reply.
  - Filter: only `change` triggers a fetch. `Show all` clears the value and fetches once without dispatching an event.
  - Rooms and the first list fetch both start at once, without waiting for each other.

**Minor findings (not failing)**
1. `app.js:164`, `179`, `184`, `188`, `191`, `192` start async calls without catching their errors. `request()` itself never rejects. But if a 200 reply's `bookings` array holds a `null` entry, `bookingText` throws inside `renderBookings`, and the browser logs it as an uncaught promise rejection.
2. `app.js:95-107` and `app.js:113-125` repeat the same steps. Each checks for no reply, then for the wrong status, then pulls an array out of the body or shows `Request failed.`

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — one closure with small single-purpose functions, shallow nesting, new payload/items built rather than mutated
naming: 9 — clear, consistent names (request, errorMessage, bookingItem, listSequence, NO_REPLY)
duplication: 8 — loadRooms and loadList repeat the same reply-checking steps
size: 10 — 193-line file, every function well under 50 lines
errors: 8 — every spec error path has a friendly one-line message; async calls are left uncaught, so a malformed booking entry becomes an uncaught rejection
tests: n/a — the testing section writes the tests
security: 10 — text only via textContent/append, path-only URLs, no secrets
leftovers: 10 — no console, debug code or TODOs; comments are explanatory only
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/public/app.js:164 add a `.catch` that shows a message for the async calls at 164/179/184/188/191/192 (or guard each booking entry in renderBookings at :77), so a bad booking entry cannot become an uncaught rejection
- /root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/public/app.js:95 move the shared no-reply / wrong-status / pull-array-from-body steps (95-107 and 113-125) into one helper, e.g. `readArray(reply, key)` that returns the array or null after showing the error
